podcast.title: Southwest Airlines Baggy Pants Incident (2011)
podcast.body: On September 1, 2011, Billie Joe Armstrong of Green Day was removed from a Southwest Airlines flight from San Francisco to Burbank. A flight attendant chastised him about his baggy pants, and despite his protests, the attendant insisted he pull them up or be removed from the plane. He refused and was subsequently thrown off, though the airline later apologized and placed him on the next available flight. "Pull your pants up or you're getting off the plane. He didn't. And he was thrown off."

podcast.title: Southwest Airlines Removal (2011)
podcast.body: On September 1, 2011, Billie Joe Armstrong was removed from a Southwest Airlines flight from San Francisco to Burbank after an altercation over his baggy pants. A flight attendant chastised him about his attire, and despite his retort, "don't you have better things to do than worry about my baggy pants?", the attendant insisted he pull up his pants or be removed. He refused and was subsequently thrown off the plane, though the airline later apologized and placed him on the next flight. "He said to have replied, don't you have better things to do than worry about my baggy pants?"

podcast.title: Family Life and Marriage
podcast.body: Billy Joe Armstrong met Adrian Nessor in 1990 through her brother, professional skateboarder Steve Nessor. Adrian brought stability to Armstrong's life during a difficult period with previous girlfriends. They married on July 2nd, 1994, and Adrian discovered she was pregnant just one day later on July 3rd, 1994. "Billy Joe Armstrong met Adrian Nessor in 1990 through her brother, who is the sister of professional skateboarder Steve Nessor. She was exactly when Armstrong needed. He'd been going through some hard times with girlfriends and she brought some stability to the situation. They were married on July 2nd, 1994, and on July 3rd, 1994, one day later, Adrian found out that she was pregnant."

podcast.title: Musical Offspring
podcast.body: Billy Joe Armstrong has two sons, Joseph Marciano Armstrong (Joey), born February 28th, 1995, and named after Joey Ramone, and Jacob Danger Armstrong, born September 12th, 1998. Both sons have followed their father into music. "And on February 28th, 1995, Joseph Marciano Armstrong came into the world. He's called Joey after Joey Ramon. Another song, Jacob Danger Armstrong. Yeah, his middle name is Danger. Came along on September 12th of 1998. Both boys took after their father."

xref.title: Billie Joe Armstrong's Marshall Rig
xref.body: Billie Joe Armstrong of Green Day is known for using various configurations of Marshall Super Lead heads and cabinets. This specific setup contributes to the band's signature sound heard on their recordings. "Billy Joe, I'm strong of Green Day uses various combinations of Marshall Super Lead heads and cabinets, and that's what we hear on this track."

xref.title: Billy Joe Armstrong's Alias
xref.body: Billie Joe Armstrong, Green Day's frontman, is known to have written songs under the alias "Will Him Think." This fact, along with his ownership of Adeline Records (which released The Network's album), contributes to the widespread suspicion that Green Day is behind The Network, despite Armstrong's denials. "It is a fact that Billy Joe has written songs under the alias Will Him Think."

xref.title: Confirmed Green Day Side Project
xref.body: Foxboro Hot Tubs is a "Garage Band side project" that Green Day undertook with friends to "blow up some creative steam" following their work on the American Idiot album. Unlike other pseudonymous projects, Green Day has been completely transparent about this identity, with Billie Joe Armstrong explicitly stating, "The only similarity between Foxboro Hot Tops and Green Day is that we are the same band." They even performed live unmasked, sometimes covering songs by The Network, their other suspected alter ego. "The only similarity between Foxboro Hot Tops and Green Day is that we are the same band, said Billy Joe Armstrong."

xref.title: Inspiration for American Idiot
xref.body: Billie Joe Armstrong was "apoplectic" about the policies and actions of George Bush's administration, particularly concerning the United States' involvement in "unnecessary wars overseas." He channeled these intense feelings into the creation of *American Idiot*, transforming his political frustrations into a critically and commercially successful quasi-concept album. "By this time, Billy Joe Armstrong was apoplectic about how George Bush was running the United States and prosecuting unnecessary wars overseas."

xref.title: Suspected Green Day Identity
xref.body: The Network, despite denials from Billie Joe Armstrong, is widely suspected to be a pseudonymous project of Green Day. Evidence includes Armstrong's ownership of their label, Adeline Records, biographical lyrical references on their album Money Money 2020, visual similarities (such as "The Snew's nose" to Tré Cool's), the band's website being registered to Green Day Inc., and their single live performance opening for Green Day on October 13, 2005. "No idea who these people are, but it's widely suspected that all three members of Green Day are somehow involved."
